qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the USDA in regulating hemp production according to the 2018 Farm Bill?
How can state departments of agriculture participate in hemp regulation under the USDA's interim final rule?
What happens if a state or tribal territory does not have a USDA-approved hemp production plan?
short_answers: Regulates hemp producers without state plans

annotations.long_answer: The USDA is responsible for establishing a regulatory plan for hemp production as stated in the 2018 Farm Bill. State departments of agriculture can participate in hemp regulation by submitting plans to the USDA for monitoring and regulating the domestic production of hemp. If a state or tribal territory does not have a USDA-approved hemp production plan, the USDA's interim final rule establishes a federal licensing plan to regulate hemp producers in those areas.

knowledge.content: The 2018 Farm Bill states that hemp production shall be subject to a hemp production regulatory plan established by the USDA, the states, or tribal governments. On October 31, 2019, the USDA issued an interim final rule establishing the domestic hemp production regulatory program to facilitate the legal production of hemp, as set forth in the 2018 Farm Bill. Under the interim final rule, state departments of agriculture and tribal governments may submit plans for monitoring and regulating the domestic production of hemp to the USDA for approval. The interim final rule establishes a federal licensing plan for regulating hemp producers in states and tribal territories that do not have their own USDA-approved plans.

qa_pairs.question: How can financial institutions support customers with limited branch access during COVID-19?
What payment accommodations can be offered to borrowers affected by COVID-19?
Will financial institutions face criticism for modifying loan terms for customers affected by COVID-19?

annotations.long_answer: Financial institutions can support customers by providing alternative service options to those who have limited ability to access branches. Institutions can offer payment accommodations such as allowing borrowers to defer or skip payments or extending the payment due date to avoid delinquencies and negative credit bureau reporting. No, prudent efforts to modify the terms on new or existing loans for affected low- and moderate-income customers, small businesses, and small farms will receive CRA consideration and not be subject to examiner criticism.

knowledge.content: Providing alternative service options to customers in light of limited ability to access branches;

Offering payment accommodations, such as allowing borrowers to defer or skip payments or extending the payment due date, which would avoid delinquencies and negative credit bureau reporting, caused by COVID-19-related issues.

The agencies emphasize that prudent efforts to modify the terms on new or existing loans for affected low- and moderate-income customers, small businesses, and small farms will receive CRA consideration and not be subject to examiner criticism.

qa_pairs.question: How can FDICconnect Coordinators manage access to the Banker Engagement Site for other users?
What steps should be taken if a user encounters issues signing into FDICconnect?
What is the role of BES Administrators in managing access permissions?

annotations.long_answer: FDICconnect Coordinators can manage access to the Banker Engagement Site (BES) for other users by accessing the Business Center Menu, expanding the Coordinator Functions Menu, and selecting 'Manage Transactions'. If a user encounters issues signing into FDICconnect, they should contact the FDIC through the Contact Us link provided on the site. BES Administrators are responsible for managing permissions for BES Contributor Access.

knowledge.content: FDICconnect Coordinators will access the Banker Engagement Site (BES) through the FDICconnect Business Center (FDICconnect), and will grant other users’ access to BES through the “Manage Transactions” function.
All users should contact the FDIC through the Contact Us link if they encounter any issues signing in to FDICconnect.
Designated BES Administrators manage permissions for BES Contributor Access. Bank Contributors are individuals who typically respond to FDIC requests for information.

annotations.long_answer:
FDICconnect Coordinators can manage access to the Banker Engagement Site (BES) for other users by accessing the Business Center Menu, expanding the Coordinator Functions Menu, and selecting 'Manage Transactions'. They can then set up BES access for each user through this function.

If a user encounters issues signing into FDICconnect, they should contact the FDIC through the Contact Us link provided on the site.

BES Administrators are responsible for managing permissions for BES Contributor Access. They ensure that users are assigned the appropriate roles and manage permissions accordingly.

The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), the National Credit Union Administration, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (collectively, the Agencies) are issuing this joint statement...

qa_pairs.question: What are the statutory requirements for banks to establish a BSA/AML compliance program?
How do federal banking agencies ensure banks comply with BSA/AML requirements?
Why is a risk-based compliance program important for banks?

annotations.long_answer: Under section 8(s) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and section 206 of the Federal Credit Union Act, federal banking agencies have prescribed regulations requiring each bank to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the requirements of the BSA. Federal banking agencies review banks' BSA/AML compliance programs during each examination cycle to ensure compliance with the requirements of the BSA. A risk-based compliance program is crucial because it enables a bank to allocate compliance resources commensurate with its risk, helping to identify and report potential money laundering, terrorist financing, and other illicit financial activity.

knowledge.content: Under existing statutory requirements, specifically section 8(s) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and section 206 of the Federal Credit Union Act, the federal banking agencies have prescribed regulations requiring each bank to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the requirements of the BSA (collectively, these procedures form the basis of each bank’s “BSA/AML compliance program”).
In addition, pursuant to these statutes, the federal banking agencies review banks’ BSA/AML compliance programs during each examination cycle.

To assure that BSA/AML compliance programs are reasonably designed to meet the requirements of the BSA, banks structure their compliance programs to be risk-based and to identify and report potential money laundering, terrorist financing, and other illicit financial activity. A risk-based compliance program enables a bank to allocate compliance resources commensurate with its risk. A bank’s well-developed risk assessment is a critical part of sound risk management and assists examiners.

qa_pairs.question: What types of deposit accounts are insured by the FDIC?
Is FDIC deposit insurance available for all financial institutions?
What assurances does the FDIC provide to consumers about their deposits?

annotations.long_answer: In FDIC-insured banks, the FDIC insures money in deposit products, which include checking accounts, NOW accounts (negotiable order of withdrawal), savings accounts, money market deposit accounts (MMDAs), and time deposits like certificates of deposit (CDs). FDIC deposit insurance is only available for money deposited in an FDIC-insured bank. The FDIC provides assurance that money deposited in an FDIC-insured institution is backed by the full faith and credit of the United States government, ensuring that the deposited money is safe.

Sin embargo, el seguro de depósito de la FDIC sólo está disponible para dinero depositado en un banco asegurado por la FDIC.

short_answers: Covers accounts up to the limit

qa_pairs.question: What types of account ownership categories are covered under FDIC insurance?

annotations.long_answer: The standard insurance coverage amount provided by the FDIC is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each category of account ownership. If a bank fails, the FDIC insurance covers the accounts of depositors at insured banks up to the insurance coverage limit, including both principal and interest up to the date of the bank's closure. The FDIC insurance covers various categories of account ownership including individual accounts, joint accounts, retirement accounts, and revocable trust accounts.

knowledge.content: El monto estándar del seguro de depósito es $250,000 por depositante, por banco asegurado para cada una de las categorías de titularidad de cuenta: cuentas individuales, conjuntas, cuentas de retiro y cuentas de fideicomiso revocable.

En el improbable caso de que su banco quiebre, el seguro de la FDIC cubre las cuentas de los depositantes en los bancos asegurados hasta el límite de la cobertura del seguro, incluso el capital y los intereses a la fecha del cierre del banco.

El monto estándar del seguro de depósito es $250,000 por depositante, por banco asegurado para cada una de las categorías de titularidad de cuenta: cuentas individuales, conjuntas, cuentas de retiro y cuentas de fideicomiso revocable.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the FDIC in consumer protection?
How can consumers contact the FDIC for inquiries?
What services are available for consumers with hearing impairments to contact the FDIC?

annotations.long_answer: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) plays a role in consumer protection by insuring deposits in banks and savings associations in the event that the institution fails. Consumers can contact the FDIC for inquiries through their toll-free call center at 1-877-ASK-FDIC (1-877-275-3342). Consumers with hearing impairments can contact the FDIC using the numbers 1-800-925-4618 or (703) 562-2289.

knowledge.content: La FDIC asegura los depósitos en bancos y asociaciones de ahorro y crédito en el evento de que la institución quiebre. La FDIC también examina y supervisa los bancos regulados estatalmente y que no son miembros del Sistema de la Reserva Federal, fomentando la confianza de consumidor en el sistema bancario.

Centro de llamadas gratuitas: 1-877-ASK-FDIC (1-877-275-3342) Nuestro horario es de lunes a viernes, de 8 a. m. a 6 p. m. hora del Este (excepto feriados federales), sábado, de 8 a. m. a 1 p. m. y domingo cerrado
Personas con deficiencias auditivas: 1-800-925-4618 o (703) 562-2289

annotations.long_answer:
The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) plays a role in consumer protection by insuring deposits in banks and savings associations in the event that the institution fails. Additionally, the FDIC examines and supervises state-regulated banks that are not members of the Federal Reserve System to promote consumer confidence in the banking system.

Consumers can contact the FDIC for inquiries through their toll-free call center at 1-877-ASK-FDIC (1-877-275-3342). The call center operates Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern Time (except federal holidays), Saturday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., and is closed on Sundays.

Consumers with hearing impairments can contact the FDIC using the numbers 1-800-925-4618 or (703) 562-2289.

The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Federal Reserve), the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) (collectively, the Agencies) are issuing this joint statement.

The purpose of the joint statement is to address due diligence questions raised by banks related to Bank Secrecy Act/Anti-Money Laundering (BSA/AML) regulatory requirements for customers whom banks may consider to be politically exposed persons (PEPs).

The organizations that collaborated to issue the joint statement are the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

qa_pairs.question: How can artificial intelligence enhance BSA/AML compliance programs in banks?
What is the purpose of pilot programs in the context of BSA/AML compliance?
Will a bank face supervisory action if a pilot program exposes gaps in their BSA/AML compliance program?

annotations.long_answer: Artificial intelligence can enhance BSA/AML compliance programs by strengthening compliance approaches and enhancing transaction monitoring systems. Pilot programs are used to test and validate the effectiveness of innovative approaches in conjunction with existing BSA/AML processes. No, a bank will not necessarily face supervisory action if a pilot program exposes gaps in their BSA/AML compliance program.

knowledge.content: Some banks are also experimenting with artificial intelligence and digital identity technologies applicable to their BSA/AML compliance programs. These innovations and technologies can strengthen BSA/AML compliance approaches, as well as enhance transaction monitoring systems.
Pilot programs undertaken by banks, in conjunction with existing BSA/AML processes, are an important means of testing and validating the effectiveness of innovative approaches.
Pilot programs that expose gaps in a BSA/AML compliance program will not necessarily result in supervisory action.

annotations.long_answer:
Artificial intelligence can enhance BSA/AML compliance programs by strengthening compliance approaches and enhancing transaction monitoring systems. These technologies help protect the financial system against illicit financial activity and maximize the utilization of banks' compliance resources.

Pilot programs are used to test and validate the effectiveness of innovative approaches in conjunction with existing BSA/AML processes. They serve as an important means for banks to experiment and assess new technologies or methods without fear of supervisory criticism if they prove unsuccessful.

No, a bank will not necessarily face supervisory action if a pilot program exposes gaps in their BSA/AML compliance program. The Agencies do not intend to criticize banks for pilot programs that reveal such gaps.

qa_pairs.question: What communication practices should insured banks adopt to minimize customer confusion about deposit and non-deposit products?
short_answers: Minimize confusion about deposit and non-deposit products

annotations.long_answer: Insured banks should confirm and monitor that crypto companies do not misrepresent the availability of deposit insurance. Non-bank entities should clearly and conspicuously state that they are not an insured bank, identify the insured bank(s) where customer funds may be held, and communicate that crypto assets are not FDIC-insured products and may lose value. Insured banks should ensure communications related to deposit insurance are clear and conspicuous, particularly when involved with non-bank entities offering both deposit products and non-deposit products like crypto assets.

knowledge.content: In their dealings with crypto companies, insured banks should confirm and monitor that these companies do not misrepresent the availability of deposit insurance in order to measure and control risks to the bank, and should take appropriate action to address such misrepresentations.

Non-bank entities, such as crypto companies, that advertise or offer FDIC-insured products in relationships with insured banks could reduce consumer confusion by clearly, conspicuously: (a) stating that they are not an insured bank; (b) identifying the insured bank(s) where any customer funds may be held on deposit; and (c) communicating that crypto assets are not FDIC-insured products and may lose value.

qa_pairs.question: What concerns does the FDIC have regarding crypto assets offered by insured banks?
How might inaccurate representations about FDIC deposit insurance by non-banks affect customers?
What confusion might customers have about the application of FDIC deposit insurance?

annotations.long_answer: The FDIC is concerned about the risks of consumer confusion or harm arising from crypto assets offered by, through, or in connection with insured depository institutions. Inaccurate representations about deposit insurance by non-banks, including crypto companies, may confuse the non-bank’s customers and cause those customers to mistakenly believe they are protected against any type of loss. Customers can be confused about when FDIC deposit insurance applies.

knowledge.content: The FDIC is concerned about the risks of consumer confusion or harm arising from crypto assets offered by, through, or in connection with insured depository institutions (insured banks). Risks are elevated when a non-bank entity offers crypto assets to the non-bank’s customers, while also offering an insured bank’s deposit products.

Inaccurate representations about deposit insurance by non-banks, including crypto companies, may confuse the non-bank’s customers and cause those customers to mistakenly believe they are protected against any type of loss.

More broadly, customers can be confused about: When FDIC deposit insurance applies. In the unlikely event of an insured-bank failure, the FDIC protects depositors of insured banks against the loss of their deposits, up to at least $250,000.

qa_pairs.question: What is the new maximum insurance coverage for trust account holders with five or more beneficiaries starting April 1, 2024?
Does the new insurance coverage limit apply to both new and existing trust accounts?
How can depositors inquire about the changes to trust account insurance coverage?

annotations.long_answer: Starting April 1, 2024, the maximum insurance coverage for a trust account holder with five or more beneficiaries is $1,250,000 per holder for all trust accounts maintained at the same bank. Yes, the new insurance coverage limit of $1,250,000 applies to both new and existing trust accounts for all deposit products, including CDs, regardless of the purchase or maturity date. Depositors can inquire about the changes to trust account insurance coverage by using the Deposit Insurance Form or by calling the FDIC at 1-877-275-3342 or 1-877-ASK-FDIC.

knowledge.content: A partir del 1 de abril de 2024, la cobertura máxima del seguro para un titular de fideicomiso con cinco o más beneficiarios es de $1,250,000 por titular para todas las cuentas de fideicomiso (incluyendo cuentas POD/ITF, fideicomisos revocables e irrevocables) mantenidas en el mismo banco.

Este cambio de cobertura se aplica tanto a las cuentas de fideicomiso nuevas como a las existentes, para todos los productos de depósito, incluidos los CDs, independientemente de la fecha de compra o vencimiento.
¿Preguntas? Puede enviar su consulta usando el Formulario del Seguro de Depósito. También puede llamar a la FDIC al 1-877-275-3342 o 1-877-ASK-FDIC.

qa_pairs.question: What are some of the key risks associated with crypto-assets that banking organizations should be aware of?
Why is there a concern about legal uncertainties in the crypto-asset sector for banking organizations?
How might crypto-asset companies misrepresent their services to banking organizations?

annotations.long_answer: Banking organizations should be aware of several key risks associated with crypto-assets, including the risk of fraud and scams among crypto-asset sector participants, legal uncertainties related to custody practices, redemptions, and ownership rights, and inaccurate or misleading representations and disclosures by crypto-asset companies. There is concern about legal uncertainties in the crypto-asset sector for banking organizations because these uncertainties relate to custody practices, redemptions, and ownership rights, some of which are currently the subject of legal processes and proceedings. Crypto-asset companies might misrepresent their services to banking organizations by providing inaccurate or misleading representations and disclosures, including misrepresentations regarding federal deposit insurance.

How can a facilitator use video vignettes to enhance discussion in a compliance meeting?

annotations.long_answer: The facilitator acts as a neutral party who provides structure to the meeting, guides information-sharing among participants, ensures everyone has an opportunity to contribute, and helps clarify goals and objectives. Limiting the number of active participants allows everyone to contribute effectively while keeping the discussion time to less than two hours. A facilitator can select a video vignette and accompanying challenge cards for participants to view and discuss.

knowledge.content: • be a neutral party who provides structure to the meeting and the discussion to meet the group’s goals and objectives. • guide information-sharing among the participants, ensure that all participants have an opportunity to contribute, and help participants clarify their goals and objectives for the discussion. • ensure that discussions move forward and are focused on the issue at hand.
2. Limit the number of active participants. Limiting participation will allow for all to contribute while keeping the anticipated discussion time to less than two hours.

3. Select a video vignette and the accompanying challenge cards for participants to view and discuss. The facilitator may use the perspectives of a character in the vignette as the focal point for the discussion (e.g., the Bank IT Manager).

knowledge.content: Under section 8(s) of the FDIA and section 206(q) of the FCUA, each of the Agencies is directed to prescribe regulations requiring each insured depository institution to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to assure and monitor the institution’s compliance with the requirements of the BSA (collectively, these procedures form the basis of each institution’s “BSA/AML compliance program”).

Sections 8(s) and 206(q) require that each Agency’s examination of an institution include a review of the institution’s BSA/AML compliance program and that reports of examination describe any problem with the BSA/AML compliance program.

If an institution fails to establish and maintain a BSA/AML compliance program, or fails to correct any problem with the BSA/AML compliance program, the Agencies will tailor actions to address the deficiencies specific to the institution.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of an issuing bank in the context of prepaid cards?
Who is responsible for designing and managing a prepaid card program?
What are the regulatory references for issuing banks handling prepaid cards?

annotations.long_answer: The issuing bank is the entity that authorizes the use of the prepaid card. A third-party program manager is responsible for designing, managing, and operating a prepaid card program. The regulatory references for issuing banks handling prepaid cards include 31 CFR 1010.

knowledge.content: The term “issuing bank” used in this guidance means the bank that authorizes use of the prepaid card. Usually the issuing bank is the bank that has its name printed on the back of a prepaid card. A bank includes any commercial bank, savings association, or credit union, and branch of a foreign bank.

For purposes of this guidance, a third-party program manager is a company that designs, manages and operates a prepaid card program and contracts with a bank to issue prepaid cards under the program and to process transactions conducted using those cards. The third-party program manager also provides customer service and card distribution (sales).

See 31 CFR 1010.100(d). 2 31 USC 5318(l). 3 68 Federal Register (FR) 25090 (May 9, 2003) codified at 31 CFR 1020.220 (Treasury); 12 CFR 21.21 (OCC); 12 CFR 208.62(b)(2) and 211.24(j)(2) (FRB); 12 CFR 326 (FDIC); and 12 CFR 748.2 (NCUA).

annotations.long_answer:
The issuing bank is the entity that authorizes the use of the prepaid card. It is usually the bank that has its name printed on the back of the prepaid card. An issuing bank can be a commercial bank, savings association, credit union, or a branch of a foreign bank.

A third-party program manager is responsible for designing, managing, and operating a prepaid card program. They contract with a bank to issue prepaid cards under the program and process transactions conducted using those cards. They also provide customer service and card distribution.

The regulatory references for issuing banks handling prepaid cards include 31 CFR 1010.100(d) for the definition of a bank, and other regulations such as 31 USC 5318(l), 31 CFR 1020.220, 12 CFR 21.21, 12 CFR 208.62(b)(2) and 211.24(j)(2), 12 CFR 326, and 12 CFR 748.2.

knowledge.content: On September 27, 2018, the FBAs and FinCEN issued an Order granting an exemption from the requirements of the CIP rules implementing section 326 of the USA PATRIOT Act, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(l), for loans extended by banks (and their subsidiaries) subject to the FBAs’ jurisdiction only to commercial customers to facilitate premium finance lending.

The consortium included the following banks: Pacific Enterprise Bank; BankDirect Capital Finance, LLC – BankDirect Capital Finance, a Division of Texas Capital Bank, N.A.; Premium Assignment Corporation, a subsidiary of SunTrust Bank; First Insurance Funding Corp.; AFCO Credit Corporation – AFCO Acceptance Corporation- Prime Rate Premium Finance Corp., subsidiaries of Branch Banking & Trust Company (BB&T); and Metabank (its AFS/IBEX division).
The Request Letters asserted that there is no need to apply the CIP rules to insurance premium finance lending because this activity presents a low risk of money laundering.

annotations.long_answer: The primary purpose of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), as outlined in 31 USC § 5311, is to require certain reports or records that have a high degree of usefulness in criminal, tax, or regulatory investigations or proceedings, or in the conduct of intelligence or counterintelligence activities, including analysis, to protect against international terrorism. Under the BSA, the term 'bank' is defined in 31 CFR 1010. Examples of interagency statements related to the BSA mentioned in the content include the October 3, 2018, Interagency Statement on Sharing Bank Secrecy Act Resources and the December 3, 2018, Joint Statement on Innovative Efforts to Combat Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing.

knowledge.content: stated in 31 USC § 5311, the purpose of the BSA is to require certain reports or records where they have a high degree of usefulness in criminal, tax, or regulatory investigations or proceedings, or in the conduct of intelligence or counterintelligence activities, including analysis, to protect against international terrorism.

Under the BSA the term “bank” is defined in 31 CFR 1010.100(d) and includes each agent, agency, branch or office within the United States of banks, savings associations, credit unions, and foreign banks.

The agencies take a careful and cautious approach to current or proposed crypto-asset-related activities and exposures at each banking organization due to the significant risks highlighted by recent failures of several large crypto-asset companies. Banking organizations are neither prohibited nor discouraged from providing banking services related to crypto-assets.

knowledge.content: The agencies are supervising banking organizations that may be exposed to risks stemming from the crypto-asset sector and carefully reviewing any proposals from banking organizations to engage in activities that involve crypto-assets. Through the agencies’ case-by-case approaches to date, the agencies continue to build knowledge, expertise, and understanding of the risks crypto-assets may pose to banking organizations, their customers, and the broader U.S. financial system.

Given the significant risks highlighted by recent failures of several large crypto-asset companies, the agencies continue to take a careful and cautious approach related to current or proposed crypto-asset-related activities and exposures at each banking organization.

The agencies are supervising banking organizations that may be exposed to risks from the crypto-asset sector and are carefully reviewing any proposals from these organizations to engage in activities involving crypto-assets. They are building knowledge and understanding of the risks posed by crypto-assets through a case-by-case approach.

The agencies take a careful and cautious approach to current or proposed crypto-asset-related activities and exposures at each banking organization due to the significant risks highlighted by recent failures of several large crypto-asset companies.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the FAQs related to the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA)?

short_answers: Money services, brokers, and mutual funds.

annotations.long_answer: Yes, a financial institution can maintain an account or customer relationship if it receives a written 'keep open' request from law enforcement, even if suspicious or potentially illicit activity has been identified. The FAQs are intended to provide clarification and do not alter existing BSA/AML legal or regulatory requirements. Entities subject to SAR requirements include banks, casinos and card clubs, money services businesses, brokers or dealers in securities, mutual funds, insurance companies, and futures commission merchants.

knowledge.content: Can a financial institution maintain an account or customer relationship for which it has received a written 'keep open' request from law enforcement, even though the financial institution has identified suspicious or potentially illicit activity?

The answers to these FAQs neither alter existing BSA/AML legal or regulatory requirements, nor establish new supervisory expectations; they were developed in response to recent Bank Secrecy Act Advisory Group (BSAAG) recommendations, as described in more detail in FinCEN’s Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) on Anti-Money Laundering Program Effectiveness, published in September 2020.

Financial institutions subject to SAR requirements include: Banks (31 CFR § 1020.320), Casinos and Card Clubs (31 CFR § 1021.320), Money Services Businesses (31 CFR § 1022.320), Brokers or Dealers in Securities (31 CFR § 1023.320), Mutual Funds (31 CFR § 1024.320), Insurance Companies (31 CFR § 1025.320), Futures Commission Merchants.

qa_pairs.question: What documentation is required when opening an account for a foreign business without an identification number?
What are the methods a bank can use to verify a customer's identity under its Customer Identification Program (CIP)?
Can a bank rely on another financial institution to perform its Customer Identification Program (CIP) procedures?

annotations.long_answer: When opening an account for a foreign business or enterprise that does not have an identification number, the bank must request alternative government-issued documentation certifying the existence of the business or enterprise. A bank’s CIP must contain procedures for verifying the identity of the customer and describe when the bank will verify customer identity through documentary methods, non-documentary methods, or a combination of both. A bank’s CIP may include procedures specifying when a bank will rely on the performance by another financial institution of the procedures of the bank’s CIP with respect to any customer of the bank that is opening, or has opened, an account or has established a similar formal banking or business relationship.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the joint statement issued by the Federal Reserve, FDIC, NCUA, and OCC?
short_answers: Set policy for issuing cease and desist orders

qa_pairs.question: Which agencies are involved in issuing the joint statement on BSA/AML enforcement?
Under which sections of law does the joint statement describe BSA/AML compliance provisions?

annotations.long_answer: The joint statement sets forth the Agencies' policy on when a mandatory cease and desist order will be issued for noncompliance with certain Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money laundering requirements, particularly in relation to specific compliance provisions in section 8(s) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and section 206(q) of the Federal Credit Union Act. The agencies involved in issuing the joint statement are the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. qa_pairs.question: What is an 'acuerdo por morosidad' and how does it affect federal student loans?
How does a 'reasonable accommodation' function in housing for individuals with disabilities?
What does the term 'adjudicación' refer to in the context of insurance claims?

annotations.long_answer: An 'acuerdo por morosidad' allows you to temporarily stop making payments or reduce your monthly payment amount for a certain period if you meet specific requirements. A 'reasonable accommodation' in housing involves a change in rules, policies, practices, or services so that a person with a disability has the same opportunity to use and enjoy a housing unit or common space. In the context of insurance claims, 'adjudicación' refers to the process of reviewing claims.

knowledge.content: Acuerdo por morosidad: Si usted cumple ciertos requisitos, el acuerdo por morosidad le permite dejar de hacer pagos temporalmente o reducir temporalmente el monto de su pago mensual durante un periodo determinado. Financial institutions subject to SAR requirements include: Banks (31 CFR § 1020.320), Casinos and Card Clubs (31 CFR § 1021.320), Money Services Businesses (31 CFR § 1022.320), Brokers or Dealers in Securities (31 CFR § 1023.320), Mutual Funds (31 CFR § 1024.320), Insurance Companies (31 CFR § 1025.320), Futures Commission Merchants.

qa_pairs.question: What documentation is required when opening an account for a foreign business without an identification number?
What are the methods a bank can use to verify a customer's identity under its Customer Identification Program (CIP)?
Can a bank rely on another financial institution to perform its Customer Identification Program (CIP) procedures?

annotations.long_answer: When opening an account for a foreign business or enterprise that does not have an identification number, the bank must request alternative government-issued documentation certifying the existence of the business or enterprise. A bank’s CIP must contain procedures for verifying the identity of the customer and describe when the bank will verify customer identity through documentary methods, non-documentary methods, or a combination of both. A bank’s CIP may include procedures specifying when a bank will rely on the performance by another financial institution of the procedures of the bank’s CIP with respect to any customer of the bank that is opening, or has opened, an account or has established a similar formal banking or business relationship.

qa_pairs.question: Which agencies are involved in issuing the joint statement on BSA/AML enforcement?
Under which sections of law does the joint statement describe BSA/AML compliance provisions?

annotations.long_answer: The joint statement sets forth the Agencies' policy on when a mandatory cease and desist order will be issued for noncompliance with certain Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money laundering requirements, particularly in relation to specific compliance provisions in section 8(s) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and section 206(q) of the Federal Credit Union Act. qa_pairs.question: What is an 'acuerdo por morosidad' and how does it affect federal student loans?
How does a 'reasonable accommodation' function in housing for individuals with disabilities?
What does the term 'adjudicación' refer to in the context of insurance claims?

annotations.long_answer: An 'acuerdo por morosidad' allows you to temporarily stop making payments or reduce your monthly payment amount for a certain period if you meet specific requirements. A 'reasonable accommodation' in housing involves a change in rules, policies, practices, or services so that a person with a disability has the same opportunity to use and enjoy a housing unit or common space. In the context of insurance claims, 'adjudicación' refers to the process of reviewing claims.

knowledge.content: Acuerdo por morosidad: Si usted cumple ciertos requisitos, el acuerdo por morosidad le permite dejar de hacer pagos temporalmente o reducir temporalmente el monto de su pago mensual durante un periodo determinado. qa_pairs.question: What is the role of an attorney in real estate transactions?
Who is considered a creditor in financial terms?

annotations.long_answer: In some real estate transactions, an attorney can perform functions such as drafting the real estate contract, conducting the title search, and handling the closing. A financial asset has monetary value, such as a savings account balance or cash, while a physical asset is something tangible that you own and has value.

Acreedor (o prestamista): persona, empresa u organización que presta dinero al deudor. También se refiere a la empresa que emite tarjetas de crédito.

Activo financiero: Activo con valor monetario, como el saldo en una cuenta de ahorro, el monto de dinero en efectivo en el bolsillo o el dinero en un fondo de inversión. Activo físico: Algo que usted posee, que tiene valor y que se puede ver y tocar.
